title: Interview feedback — ATOMIC format + Calibration Lab
body:
Purpose:
This doc proposes a compact, interviewer-friendly feedback format (ATOMIC) and an operational pattern for running weekly calibration labs. The goal is twofold: 1) make feedback clearer and faster to write, and 2) reduce variance between interviewers when mapping signals to a hire/no-hire recommendation. This is a working doc — open questions and TODOs at the end.

Why we need a new format:
- Current feedback notes often mix impressions, candidate quotes, role expectations, and action items in freeform blocks — hard for hiring teams to synthesize.
- We see variability across interviewers when translating behaviors into level/competency signals.
- Fast-moving hiring requires concise, normalized signals that still preserve nuance for equity and audit.

ATOMIC (recommended feedback fields) — a short checklist interviewers can complete in ~5–7 minutes after a loop: 
- A = Actionable Summary (1–2 sentences): clear, specific outcome-oriented statement. e.g., “Candidate delivered a robust approach to model-serving latency: proposed sharding + async prefetch; missed rollout monitoring detail.”
- T = Timely Evidence (timestamped/phase-specific): short bullet(s) with what the candidate actually did or said. Use quotes sparingly. e.g., “(Q2) Proposed partition key per-user for KV cache; suggested warm-up function but no monitoring plan.”
- O = Observed Behaviors (3–5 bullets): concrete behaviors tied to competency (problem decomposition, code clarity, trade-off reasoning, cross-team communication). Avoid global adjectives.
- M = Measurable Gap/Strength (map to rubric): single-line mapping to our existing competency scale (1–5) for primary competency tested. e.g., “System design: 3/5 — good decomposition, needs concrete metrics/SLIs planning.”
- I = Inclusive Notes (bias-aware prompt): mention any accommodation used/needed and a short reflection if any bias risk noted. e.g., “Needed 20s extra time for whiteboard due to peripheral vision issue; candidate performed well after.”
- C = Context & Recommendation (role fit + next step): final line with recommendation tied to role/level. e.g., “Strong IC3 systems candidate — recommend onsite for cross-functional deep-dive; consider paired design task.”

Template (paste into interviewer form):
- Actionable summary:
- Timely evidence:
  - (minute/section) short bullet
- Observed behaviors:
  - behavior 1
  - behavior 2
  - behavior 3
- Measurable mapping (competency: score 1–5):
- Inclusive notes / accommodations: 
- Context & recommendation (hire / consider / pass + reason):

Quick examples (realistic, compact):
1) Backend engineering loop (IC3):
- Actionable summary: Candidate proposed a partitioned KV cache with LRU eviction and async prefetch for hot keys; did not outline how prefetch failures are surfaced to callers.
- Timely evidence: (design) drew diagram showing shard boundaries; (follow-up) acknowledged consistency trade-offs when scaling reads.
- Observed behaviors: good decomposition, asked clarifying questions early, used quantitative reasoning for trade-offs.
- Measurable mapping: System design: 4/5; Observability: 2/5.
- Inclusive notes: candidate asked for a minute to reframe the question; performed better with that pause.
- Context & recommendation: Recommend move to final loop with focused observability question.

2) Product design / PM loop:
- Actionable summary: Candidate focused on customer outcomes and metrics, but struggled to prioritize work when given three competing roadmap items.
- Timely evidence: (Q1) Prioritized roadmap by revenue impact only, didn’t discuss tech debt or dependencies.
- Observed behaviors: strong customer empathy, less structured prioritization framework.
- Measurable mapping: Product judgment: 3/5; Prioritization: 2/5.
- Inclusive notes: non-native speaker — asked for question restatement; content strong after restatement.
- Context & recommendation: Candidate could fit a PM associate role with coaching; recommend considering for IC2 with gap plan.

Calibration lab playbook (weekly, 45–60m):
- Goal: align on scoring thresholds and common edge cases.
- Frequency: weekly during active hiring cycles (every sprint); monthly otherwise.
- Attendees: hiring managers, 2 senior interviewers per role family, 1 People Ops coordinator. Rotate panelists so not always the same voices.
- Agenda (45m):
  1) 0–5m: quick metrics snapshot (open reqs, pass rate, time-to-decision)
  2) 5–20m: read 2 anonymized ATOMIC feedbacks (from recent loops) — vote and justify
  3) 20–40m: discuss disagreements, map to rubric language, capture 2–3 clarifying rubric edits or examples
  4) 40–50m: action items (update canonical rubric examples, share one micro-training note)
  5) 50–60m: open Qs and scheduling
- Prework: People Ops anonymizes and bundles candidate feedback (remove demographic markers). Provide the primary competency to assess.
- Output: short minutes (2 bullets) and an updated example bank on Confluence.

Calibration lab governance:
- Decision rule: majority vote maps to final hiring committee guidance; dissenting voters must add a 1–2 line rationale in ATOMIC’s Context field.
- Audit: retain anonymized feedback and vote outcomes in Confluence for 7 quarters (for fairness reviews).
- Escalation: if persistent >1 level variance across labs for same role family, trigger a cross-functional rubric rewrite (task: HR-4521).

Operational notes for interviewers (fast adoption tips):
- Write the Actionable summary first — forces clarity.
- Use measured language: replace ‘smart’/‘great’ with observed behavior + example.
- Fill the Measurable mapping as a single numeric score and short phrase (don’t write a paragraph).
- Inclusive notes are required; if no accommodation used write ‘none’.
- If unsure about level, mark ‘lean towards’ and justify. Hiring manager will synthesize.

Coach snippets (for training):
- If debate centers on missing context vs. actual weakness, ask: could candidate answer this in a 15-minute follow-up? If yes, consider level-appropriate gap vs. fail.
- Use the phrase ‘observable at level X’ when justifying promotion or hire.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we require ATOMIC as mandatory in Lever form or keep as a recommended template? (Action: People Ops to consult Product & Eng hiring managers.)
- How to map ATOMIC fields into existing Lever fields without duplication? (Action: Engineering on Lever integrations — Jira HR-4521.)
- Training plan: record a 20-minute micro-training video + 2 example bundles for calibration labs (owner: Marcus Lee).
- Legal: confirm retention window meets local regs for EU candidates (owner: Elena Rodriguez).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: over-normalization may strip nuance. Mitigation: require a 1-line Context with recommendation and keep raw notes attached.
- Risk: calibration group bias (same folks dominating). Mitigation: rotate panel members and include at least one cross-team interviewer.

Next steps (30/60/90):
- 0–30 days: pilot ATOMIC on 3 open reqs across Eng, PM, Data; run 2 calibration labs; collect feedback. (Owner: People Ops)
- 30–60 days: decide on Lever integration and final template; produce micro-training + example bundles. (Owner: People Ops + Eng PM)
- 60–90 days: roll ATOMIC company-wide; schedule quarterly audit of variance and closed-loop improvements. (Owner: People Ops)

Appendix: short rubric mapping cheat-sheet (single-line entries to copy into the template):
- 1: critical gap (candidate cannot perform responsibilities at level)
- 2: needs substantial coaching / foundations missing
- 3: meets expectations with some gaps
- 4: solid performer for level
- 5: exceeds expectations / strong stretch

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact and interviewer-facing. Please comment in this doc with examples of candidate answers that should map to each numeric score in your role family.
- If you are an external recruiter, flag any candidate experiences that need accommodation; we will ensure consistent treatment.
